newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: FISCHER SAYS NO CHANGES BECAUSE OF DENG'S DEATH
Deputy Prime Minister and acting foreign affairs minister, Tim Fischer, says the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaopeng won't change Australia's relationship with China.
China's official news agency, Xinhua announced the 93-year-old died of respiratory failure shortly after midnight Australian Eastern Daylight time.
It's believed he'd suffered the advanced stages of Parkinson's disease, with complications from lung infections.
Deng will be remembered as the man who tore down the disasterous economic legacy of Chairman Mao and in 1978 introduced reforms which has transformed China.
He'll also be remembered for the bloody suppression in Tianamen Square in 1989.
Tim Fischer says Xiaopeng helped boost economic growth through North-east Asia.
BELL CONSIDERING APPEAL AFTER EXTRADITION DECISION
In South Africa, lawyers for alleged paedophile, Phillip Bell aren't saying if they'll lodge an appeal after yesterday's court decision which found Mr Bell should be extradited to Australia.
Mr Bell is facing hundreds of child sex abuse charges.
Senior police close to the case say they believe a legal challenge is inevitable.
Mr Bell has 15-days to lodge an appeal, and if he does it could delay his return to Australia for months.
The South African magistrate rejected attempts by Mr Bell to contest dozens of the 215 outstanding warrants against him, ruling he should return to Australia to face all outstanding allegations.
SAFEGUARDS FOR REEF DURING TANDEM THRUST
The Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority has released a series of strict environmental safeguards for troops taking part in next month's Exercise Tandem Thrust.
Authority Spokesman, Craig Sambell, says the safeguards include aircraft flight restrictions, waste discharge regulations, and procedures for protecting marine wildlife.
He says the strict guidelines have been endorsed by both the Australian and US Defence Forces.
BUSINESS INVESTMENT CURBS RECESSION
Economic forecasters, Access Economics, says Australia would be in recession if it wasn't for current levels of strong business investment.
In its latest monthly "Economics Monitor" the group's described business investment as "booming".
It's also confident investment will continue to rise following yesterday's release of imports figures for January.
They show a 29-percent surge in offshore purchases of capital items ... lifting the overall value of imports to six per cent for month to a one-and-a-half year high.
GUARANTEES URGED ON MEAT AND DAIRY EXPORTS
A Japanese dairy company says the outbreak of Anthrax in Victoria is a serious issue for Asian Pacific Markets.
The President of Meiji Milk products company, Mr Nakayama, is urging the Federal Government to guarantee the safety of all Australian meat and dairy products.
Mr Nakayama says the south-east Asian market is very sensitive following mad cow disease in Britain, so some assurance from Government is necessary.
Meiji Milk Products is a joint partner with Mitsubishi and Murray Goulburn in a 50 million dollar infant formula plant which was officially opened at Cobram yesterday.
GREENPEACE VIGIL TO WATCH NUCLEAR WASTE SHIPMENT
Greenpeace claims the Federal Government hasn't given Australians enough information about a shipment of nuclear waste passing through waters off Tasmania.
The group is sending out a spotter plane this morning to check the route of the shipment of 40 blocks of highly radioactive waste from France to Japan.
The waste is being carried by British ship - the Pacific Teal, and Greenpeace says she's thought to be close to entering Australian waters.
Greenpeace campaigner Damian Moglen, says the flight's been organised to track the waste because the government hasn't supplied adequate details about it's route for passing Australia.
MEASURES TO STOP SEX OFFENDERS WORKING IN SCHOOLS
The Victorian government has put a range of measures in place to prevent sex offenders working in Victorian schools.
So far, 17,000 people have undergone police checks, including relief teachers and contractors who work on school grounds.
Existing teachers who are seeking a promotion or transfer will also be checked.
The Education Minister, Phil Gude, says the regulations are being adopted by other states to stop sex offenders working in the department.
He says teachers wrongly accused of a sex offence and found NOT guilty by a court will be given a full copy of the police brief and court transcript
